question: How much does Pilates teacher training cost?
answer: Mat, Reformer and Barre teacher training each cost £2,200. That includes the online Human Movement course, five in-person days, your manual, the video library, all workshops and all exams. There are no extra fees for assessment or certification. You can pay in full or in four monthly interest-free payments.

question: Can I pay in instalments?
answer: Yes. Qualify courses can be paid in four monthly interest-free payments of £550. A double booking of two courses can be spread over six payments. CPD can be paid in two instalments. All payments are non-refundable and non-transferable.

question: Is there a discount for booking two courses?
answer: Yes. Book any two of Mat, Reformer and Barre together for £3,400, a saving of £1,000, with the option of six monthly interest-free payments.

question: Is there a discount if I already have a fitness qualification?
answer: Students with an existing Level 3 fitness qualification receive £400 off. Email a copy of your certificate to info@thepilatesprogramme.co.uk and we will send you a discount code.

question: What is your refund policy?
answer: All payments are non-refundable and non-transferable. If something changes before your course, email us as early as you can and we will do what we can to help.

question: Are there any extra costs to plan for?
answer: Exams, your manual and assessment are included. Beyond the course fee you may want to budget for studio or equipment hire for practice hours, teacher insurance once you start teaching, and travel to Altrincham. The pricing page lists current hire rates.

question: How many practice hours do I need, and how do I organise them?
answer: After the in-person intensive you complete 30 observation hours, 25 personal study hours and 25 practice teaching hours. Most students finish in eight to twelve weeks alongside a job. You can observe classes locally or online, hire studio space and equipment at the centre, and practise teaching friends, family or a local studio. We give you a plan and support you through it.

question: What are the exams like?
answer: There are three: a 50-question multiple choice Human Movement exam, a 30-question multiple choice theory exam, and a practical exam where you teach a 45-minute class plus five random exercises over Zoom. All are included in the course fee, and you are prepared for each one during training.

question: How long does it take to become a Pilates instructor?
answer: From booking to your first paid class is typically three to four months: pre-course online study, five in-person days, then around eight weeks of practice hours and exams. Some students take longer around work and family, and that is fine.

question: Do I need Pilates experience to train as a Mat teacher?
answer: You do not need a qualification, but you should have practised Pilates regularly and enjoy it. If you are new to Pilates, we suggest attending classes for a few months first so the repertoire feels familiar.

question: Do I need access to a Reformer to train?
answer: For the in-person days, no. For your practice hours you will need regular time on a Reformer, either at a local studio, through equipment hire at our centre, or at home. If you have no access at all, Mat may be the better first course.

question: Do I need a dance background to teach Barre?
answer: No. Barre uses ballet positions but you are training to teach conditioning, not ballet. Musicality and a love of group classes matter more than dance training.

question: Should I do Mat or Reformer first?
answer: Mat gives you the fullest foundation, works anywhere and needs no equipment for practice hours. Reformer is the format most boutique studios hire for. Many students book both as a double booking and save £1,000. If you are unsure, take the 60-second course quiz.

question: Are your courses accredited?
answer: Our courses are internationally accredited by ITTAP through the Pilates Method Alliance, and The Pilates Programme is a CIMSPA Training Partner. The accreditation page explains what each body is and what it means for where you can teach.

question: What support do I get after I qualify?
answer: You keep access to the online platform and video library, you can hire studio space and equipment at the centre, you receive 10% off further training, and our jobs board lists roles from studios across Manchester, Cheshire and the North West.

question: Where do your graduates teach?
answer: Our graduates teach in boutique studios, gyms, community venues and their own businesses across the North West and beyond. The graduates page lists profiles and studios as our graduates share them.

question: What do I need before an apparatus course?
answer: Chair, Cadillac and Barrels require an existing Mat or Reformer teaching certification from any provider. Advanced Reformer requires an existing Reformer qualification. Each course includes its manual, exam, an interest-free payment plan and online platform access with a 6-week free trial.

question: How does the apparatus bundle work?
answer: Book Cadillac, Chair and Barrels together for £2,700 and Barrels is included free. You attend each course on its scheduled dates.

question: Is there a discount for past students?
answer: Yes. Past graduates receive 10% off further training and CPD. Email us with the course you trained on and we will send your code.

question: Can I attend CPD if I trained elsewhere?
answer: Yes. CPD days are open to qualified Pilates and Barre teachers from any provider.

question: How does the online CPD work?
answer: The Jumpboard CPD is on demand. After booking you receive access to the videos and notes and can complete it in your own time.

question: Can I pay for CPD in instalments?
answer: Yes. Every continuing education course, apparatus and CPD, can be paid in full or in two interest-free instalments. The manual, exams or assessment, and online platform access with a 6-week free trial are included in the price. All payments are non-refundable and non-transferable.

question: Where is the training centre?
answer: 23 Central Way, Altrincham, WA14 1RF, a short walk from Altrincham train and tram interchange with parking nearby. The centre has two floors with full apparatus and Barre fit-out, seminar screens, study spaces and a kitchen. Some courses run at partner studios in Manchester city centre.

question: Can I hire the studio for practice hours?
answer: Yes. Students can hire studio space and equipment at the centre for practice teaching and observation. Current rates are on the pricing and training centre pages.

question: Do you run weekend courses?
answer: Current cohorts run on weekdays. Check the course dates page for the latest schedule, or get notified when new dates are released.
